Unit test for {@link StringTokenizer}.

Asserts that the tokens produced by a tokenizer match {@code expected} exactly, comparing both the number of tokens and each token in order. @param expected the tokens that the tokenizer is expected to produce. @param actual the tokens actually produced by the tokenizer.

Semicolon-delimited, double-quoted input where the trim characters are configured as the ignored matcher. Surrounding whitespace is stripped and the trailing empty fields are retained because empty tokens are not ignored.
Semicolon-delimited, double-quoted input with no ignored/trim matcher. Whitespace around tokens (the trailing {@code "c "} and the single-space fields) is preserved, and empty tokens are kept.
Same configuration as {@link #testSemicolonQuotedNoneIgnoredKeepsTrailingSpace()} but with the whitespace leading a token ({@code " c"}); it is likewise preserved when no ignored/trim matcher is set.
Trim characters configured as the ignored matcher, with empty tokens ignored: surrounding whitespace is stripped and the trailing empty fields are dropped entirely.
Empty tokens are kept but returned as {@code null} because {@code setEmptyTokenAsNull(true)} is enabled.

Verifies that the {@code ListIterator} navigation can walk forward through every token with {@code hasNext()}/{@code next()} and then back through every token with {@code hasPrevious()}/{@code previous()}, visiting the same number of tokens in each direction.
tok.setTreatingEmptyAsNull(true);
Only the token count matters here; the iteration walks the list rather than checking values.
Space-delimited, double-quoted input keeping empty tokens: each run of consecutive spaces yields the intervening empty tokens, and the quoted {@code "d e"} stays intact.
Same space-delimited input as {@link #testSpaceDelimitedQuotedKeepsEmptyTokens()} but with empty tokens ignored, so only the five non-empty tokens remain.
